content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed DualMatch, which is a new method for semi-supervised learning. DualMatch introduces the hierarchical labels to learn an adaptive threshold to select highly-confident samples. Then, DualMatch build an affinity graph to perform contrastive learning to capture discriminative features. Extensive experiments demonstrate its effectiveness.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strengths

- This paper is well-written and easy to understand.
- DualMatch is well motivated and interesting.
- DualMatch achieves great performance on common benchmarks.

### Weaknesses

- The contribution of the method is rather limited, with limited novelty. It is a combination of existing technologies.
- For experiments, the effect of using coarse labels is underexplored. Extra information would help the learning, yet there is no result analysis of the proposed method without the coarse labels or the previous methods with coarse labels.
- The total objective in Eq.4 uses same weight for each loss objective, yet no ablation or reason why same weight is used is provided.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes using hierarchical label and contrastive learning to refine semi-supervised learning.  Specifically, this paper respectively generates fine-grained and coarse pseudo labels. Then it respectively uses these pseudo labels to create the affinity graphs. The final element of the affinity graph is the intersection of both fine-grained and coarse ones. Finally, the contrastive learning loss whose positive samples and negative samples are separated by the affinity graph is used for model training. Beyond contrastive learning loss, two unsupervised classification losses based on fine-grained and coarse pseudo labels are also used for training.  Besides, this paper uses a memory bank to modify the thresholds in the FixMatch framework.  Compared with FixMatch, this method achieves improved experimental results.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1) Compared with the FixMatch baseline, the proposed method achieves experimental improvement.
2) Some experimental details are shown in the appendix.

Weaknesses:
1) The contribution is not clear. First, this paper claims to use contrastive learning to promote semi-supervised learning. However, contrastive learning based methods have already been a good branch in the field of semi-supervised learning. Many existing methods have applied contrastive learning for semi-supervised learning tasks, such as CCSSL[1], Comatch[2], and co-calibration[3]. Besides, some methods have explored using the hierarchical label to refine semi-supervised learning, such as HIERMATCH[4]. It is suggested to add more discussions with these related methods and claim the contributions more precisely. 
2) Following the first problem, more methods (especially for contrastive semi-supervised learning) should be compared in the experiments. 
It seems that the claim of outperforming state-of-the-art methods is not accurate.
3) The writing and figures should be improved. Some descriptions are confusing. In figure 2, the graph matching part is not clear, the nodes in the top graph denote labels but the nodes in the bottom one are features.  In eq(7), only the edges in both graphs retrain, but in figure 2, the edges in graph g_f but not graph g_c retrain.

[1]Yang F, Wu K, Zhang S, et al. Class-Aware Contrastive Semi-Supervised Learning[C]//Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2022: 14421-14430.

[2] Li J, Xiong C, Hoi S C H. Comatch: Semi-supervised learning with contrastive graph regularization[C]//Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision. 2021: 9475-9484.

[3] Zhang Y, Zhang X, Li J, et al. Semi-supervised contrastive learning with similarity co-calibration[J]. IEEE Transactions on Multimedia, 2022.

[4]Garg A, Bagga S, Singh Y, et al. HIERMATCH: Leveraging Label Hierarchies for Improving Semi-Supervised Learning[C]//Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision. 2022: 1015-1024.

content.summary_of_the_paper: DualMatch extends FixMatch and FlexMatch with dynamic threshold learning that uses a percentile approach.  The most significant contribution is a course and fine approach to contrastive learning.  Using two independent heads for the course and fine classes seems to improve the learning rate and the number of samples required.  They enforce consistency between estimated fine and course grain class estimates, which seems to improve convergency and generalization.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper propose a novel DualMatch method, which can learn an adaptive threshold for all classes to perform instance-level prediction matching as well as discriminative features by graph matching based contrastive learning. Experiment showing there are improvements in sevearal datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Overall, the reviewer believes this work lacks novelty, and the proposed module is incremental and lacks proper justification.
First of all, the idea of adaptive thresholding is not new in SSL. It has been explored in several works (e.g., Class-Imbalanced Semi-Supervised Learning with Adaptive Thresholding, ICML'22). 

Second, the reviewer considers it is not proper to call the proposed method contrastive learning. The idea of the proposed method is to increase the degree of feature discrimination by introducing negative samples. However, the positive and negative samples are based on labels. Not sure if it is contrastive learning. Or we should call it metric learning. besides, the construction of the affinity graph is also common in metric learning. 

Although the proposed method is empirically promising, this work is quite incremental. For ICLR, it is not enough to merely show the improvement. More insight should be provided.
